title: Legal consequences on compiler not calling encryption/ decryption algorithms
content_md:
Suppose you have private data, you send that data to an encryption function, but the compiler decided to not call the function. Is your legal fault for this compiler's decision? Although a bad example, suppose you use Cesar's encryption with key 0 to encrypt and decrypt. The compiler can see that you are practically doing nothing in there (just adding 0 to the array of data), so it can decide to either not call the function, or call it, but no instruction is in there. A theoretical exampe might be in this tutorial , where you put the encrypt/ decrypt function after while(keepLooping) stop executing, aka keepLooping changed the value.
